pr_title: Remove ANSI color sequences when calculating width of display text
pr_body: Fixes #4065 This PR fixes the example shown in the issue as follows: The start positions of issue date column are aligned correctly.

issue_context.title: Wrong calculation of width of text including ANSI color sequences
issue_context.body: ### Describe the bug - gh version: 1.13.1 - OS: macOS 10.15 When showing some outputs with table writer, width of some cell is wrong. For example: In this example, the start position of 'about 3 hours ago' at issue `#19` is wrong. This is because issue labels are colorized with ANSI color sequences like `\x1b[38;2;215;58;74mbug\x1b[0m` and the logic to calculate display width of text does not consider the sequences. ### Steps to reproduce the behavior 1. Checkout some repository which has two open issues. And those issues should have different number of labels. 2. Run `gh issue list` 3. See output and confirm the start position of column of issue date is wrong ### Expected vs actual behavior - Expected: Width of display text must consider ANSI escape sequences since such sequences are actually not rendered on terminal - Actual: ANSI escape sequences are included in display text. For example, width of `(\x1b[38;2;162;238;239menhancement\x1b[0m)` is calculated as 34. ### Logs ``` U'w') { gh issue list Showing 2 of 2 open issues in rhysd/actionlint #19 Feature Request: checking for Untrusted input (enhancement) about 3 hours ago #18 "is not defined in object type" error with marketplace action (bug, false-positive) about 53 minutes ago ```
comments:
Thank you for reporting! Could have been caused by #3912. 

@bchadwic was it the intent that `gh issue list` label output is also colored? Or was the idea to only color `issue view` output

@mislav my PR #3519 should correctly take care of this because of the changes I made to https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/3519/files#diff-7cd07c3defa4823b12484e616fc8cb5f63dc01e5a9df23544634b111a8d20547 to handle this very situation.

That said, note also the closing parenthesis is the wrong color.

I reverted PR #4079 and pulled in my updated `text.Truncate` function from PR #3519, as well as fixed the closing parenthesis. Alternatively, it's be cleaner to just leave it the default color e.g., white but would be a visual change...not that coloring labels isn't already a visual change. Or, again alternatively, are the parenthesis even needed? The `tsvTablePrinter` doesn't print parenthesis. I suppose the idea with the `ttyTablePrinter` is to better delineate the labels from other columns.

review_comments:
Thank you for the straightforward fix!

Note that an older PR https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/3519/files#diff-7cd07c3defa4823b12484e616fc8cb5f63dc01e5a9df23544634b111a8d20547R15 also proposes ignoring ANSI escape sequences when measuring width of text, but uses a library that does this [without a regular expression](https://github.com/muesli/reflow/blob/9d08d19fb40b1e4b2db5e2731cdb5d318d363ba9/ansi/buffer.go#L21). I would personally vote for that approach since it might be computationally lighter. However, that PR isn't reviewed yet. Please allow us some time to decide how to proceed.
